RequirementText: LILP-REQ-DET-007 INVALID SHALL remain distinguishable from NOT ESTABLISHED. ====================================================================== 20. FORMAL CORE ====================================================================== The following abstract model expresses the minimum LILP relationship. Let the governing state at time n be: G_n = { I_n, A_n, St_n, E_n, P_n, Sc_n, J_n, T_n, C_n } where: I_n = identity A_n = authority St_n = governing state E_n = required evidence P_n = applicable policy Sc_n = scope J_n = jurisdiction T_n = temporal context C_n = contemplated effect Let Canon(x) be the declared deterministic canonicalisation function. Let H(x) be the declared cryptographic hash function. The locked state identity may be represented as: LOCK_n = H(Canon(G_n)) A material change may be represented as: DELTA_n = Compare(G_(n-1), G_n) Execution permission requires every mandatory predicate applicable to the contemplated effect to be established: PERMIT_n = I_n AND A_n AND St_n AND E_n AND P_n AND Sc_n AND J_n AND T_n AND C_n The fundamental execution invariant is: EXECUTE_n => PERMIT_n The inverse is not required: PERMIT_n does not imply that EXECUTE_n must occur. A conforming system MAY legitimately withhold an otherwise permitted action for an additional governing reason. Where PERMIT_n cannot be established: EXECUTE_n = FALSE for the contemplated consequential action. A receipt identity may be represented abstractly as: R_n = H( Canon( receipt_metadata_n || LOCK_n || DELTA_n || determination_n || execution_status_n || consequence_status_n || claim_ceiling_n ) ) Where cryptographic receipt chaining is used: R_n = H( Canon( R_(n-1) || receipt_metadata_n || LOCK_n || DELTA_n || determination_n || execution_status_n || consequence_status_n || claim_ceiling_n ) ) These equations define governance relationships. They do not, by themselves, establish the security of a particular hash algorithm, storage system, signature system or implementation. ====================================================================== 21. TECHNICAL-MIDDLE STATUS ====================================================================== This section establishes the first implementable normative object and execution model for ELIAS-LILP-STD-001 v0.1. The standard remains a WORKING DRAFT. No conformance claim SHALL be made solely from the presence of these requirements. Conformance requires the separately defined conformance and falsification procedures. ====================================================================== 22. CLAIM MODEL AND CLAIM CLASSES ====================================================================== A LILP claim is a bounded proposition whose permissible wording SHALL be constrained by the evidence preserved to support it. Minimum semantic model: CLAIM_n = { claim_id, claim_class, subject_reference, proposition, scope, temporal_scope, evidence_references, verification_method, proof_level, result, claim_ceiling } ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 22.1 CLAIM CLASSES ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The following claim classes define distinguishable properties. C1 — IDENTITY / INTEGRITY CLAIM A claim concerning byte identity, cryptographic digest, object identity or integrity relationship. Example: "The examined file matches SHA-256 X." C2 — PROVENANCE / LINEAGE CLAIM A claim concerning origin, predecessor relationship, successor relationship or recorded transformation history. C3 — STATE CLAIM A claim concerning an observed or governing state at a defined time. C4 — AUTHORITY / STANDING CLAIM A claim concerning established authority, standing, admissibility or jurisdictional validity. C5 — DETERMINATION CLAIM A claim concerning the governance determination actually reached. C6 — EXECUTION CLAIM A claim concerning whether consequential execution was withheld, attempted, completed or failed. C7 — CONSEQUENCE CLAIM A claim concerning an observed consequence resulting from or associated with execution. C8 — CONFORMANCE CLAIM A claim concerning satisfaction of specified requirements and tests under a declared LILP conformance profile. C9 — EXTERNAL VALIDATION CLAIM A claim concerning independent certification, regulatory approval, scientific validation, standards-body adoption or other external recognition. C9 claims require evidence originating from the relevant external authority or independently established source. LILP itself does not create such external recognition.

PROOF LEVELS ====================================================================== LILP proof levels describe how a bounded claim is supported. They are not universal rankings of system quality. A higher proof level for one property does not establish unrelated properties. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.1 PL0 — NOT ESTABLISHED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The available evidence is insufficient to establish the proposition. Permitted result: NOT ESTABLISHED PL0 SHALL NOT be represented as successful verification. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.2 PL1 — ATTESTED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The proposition is asserted by an identified actor, system or source, but has not been independently verified under the applicable method. Example: A provider states that a feature is enabled. This establishes the existence of the attestation when the attestation itself is preserved. It does not automatically establish the truth of the underlying proposition. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.3 PL2 — INTEGRITY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- A reproducible technical method establishes an integrity or identity relationship. Examples include: - matching cryptographic hashes; - verified signatures; - canonical byte equality. PL2 establishes only the property actually verified. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.4 PL3 — PROCEDURALLY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- The claim has been examined using a declared procedure against the relevant evidence within the controlled examination environment. The procedure, evidence and result SHALL be inspectable. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.5 PL4 — INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- A verifier sufficiently independent from the originating determination has examined the bounded claim against the relevant evidence using an identified method. The verification relationship and verification scope SHALL be disclosed. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 23.6 PL5 — INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Where reproduction is technically meaningful, an independent examiner has reproduced the relevant bounded result using the declared conditions, artifacts or procedure. PL5 SHALL NOT be claimed where the evidence package does not contain the material necessary for independent reproduction.

MANDATORY FALSIFICATION TEST SET ====================================================================== Conformance testing SHALL attempt to cause the claimed controls to fail. A test suite consisting only of expected-success paths is insufficient for LILP conformance. The following tests form the minimum general falsification set. Domain-specific profiles MAY require additional tests. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-001 — RECEIPT IDENTIFIER COLLISION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to create a second receipt using an existing receipt identifier. Expected conforming behaviour: - silent overwrite does not occur; - predecessor remains preserved; - operation refuses or creates an explicit successor/correction. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-002 — FROZEN PREDECESSOR MUTATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to represent a changed state by altering the frozen predecessor. Expected conforming behaviour: - predecessor remains unchanged; - changed condition is represented separately; - successor or correction path is used. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-003 — REVOKED AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Establish authority at T0. Then revoke that authority before consequential execution. Expected conforming behaviour: EXECUTE = FALSE for the affected consequence unless separate current authority is established. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-004 — EXPIRED AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present historically valid but expired authority. Expected conforming behaviour: Historical authority remains preservable as historical evidence. Present execution authority is not inferred from it. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-005 — MISSING REQUIRED EVIDENCE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Remove or withhold evidence required by a mandatory execution predicate. Expected conforming behaviour: HOLD, DENY, ESCALATE or NOT ESTABLISHED as governed by policy. The system does not manufacture ALLOW. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-006 — OBSERVATION / INTERPRETATION CONFLICT ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present an observation and a machine interpretation that disagree. Expected conforming behaviour: The observation and interpretation remain separately represented. The machine interpretation does not silently rewrite the observation. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-007 — TOCTOU STATE CHANGE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Establish a valid determination. Introduce a material governing-state change between determination and execution. Expected conforming behaviour: Execution is withheld pending reassessment. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-008 — CAPABILITY WITHOUT AUTHORITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Provide technical capability to perform a consequential action while withholding execution authority. Expected conforming behaviour: Technical capability remains present. EXECUTE = FALSE. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-009 — EXECUTION ATTEMPT WITHOUT CONFIRMED CONSEQUENCE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Create evidence that execution was attempted while withholding evidence that the intended consequence completed. Expected conforming behaviour: Execution attempt may be established. Completed consequence remains NOT ESTABLISHED. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-010 — UNCERTAINTY PRESERVATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Provide insufficient evidence for a required proposition. Expected conforming behaviour: NOT ESTABLISHED remains representable. The system does not force the proposition into TRUE or FALSE. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-011 — IDENTITY CONTINUITY GAP ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Present predecessor and candidate-successor objects without sufficient evidence establishing required identity continuity. Expected conforming behaviour: Continuity is not invented. Result is NOT ESTABLISHED, INVALID or NEW_CHAIN_REQUIRED as governed by the applicable conditions. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-012 — CANONICALISATION REPRODUCIBILITY ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Canonicalise and hash the same material object independently using the declared procedure. Expected conforming behaviour: Equivalent canonical objects produce the same byte identity. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-013 — BYTE TAMPER DETECTION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Alter at least one material byte in an integrity-protected artifact. Expected conforming behaviour: The altered artifact does not verify against the predecessor digest. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-014 — GOVERNANCE-GATE BYPASS ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to reach consequential execution without satisfying the declared governance gate. Expected conforming behaviour: The claimed non-bypassable restraint prevents unauthorised execution. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-015 — FAILURE / SUCCESSOR PRESERVATION ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Create a failing state and then correct the implementation through a successor. Expected conforming behaviour: The failed predecessor remains preserved. The successor is separately identifiable. The later success does not erase the earlier failure. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- LILP-TEST-016 — CLAIM-CEILING CHALLENGE ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Attempt to produce a claim broader than the evidence supports. Examples: - infer truth from hash identity; - infer present authority from historical authority; - infer consequence from execution attempt; - infer certification from self-assessed conformance. Expected conforming behaviour: The broader claim is refused, bounded or marked NOT ESTABLISHED.
